claims.text: Conventional fabrication of single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered single-phase ZrB2 typically has high porosity and microstructural defects.
The porosity and defects in conventionally sintered ZrB2 compromise its strength and long-term stability during liquid-bath exposure.
Replacing conventional sintering with SPS can reduce the required ZrB2 sintering temperature below 2300 °C.
SPS can improve ZrB2 densification and reduce its porosity.
Reduced porosity from SPS will enhance ZrB2 structural integrity and resistance to degradation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
SPS processing of ZrB2 can target a sintering-temperature range of approximately 1900–2100 °C under vacuum or an inert atmosphere.
Rapid localized Joule heating and applied pressure enhance grain-boundary diffusion and reduce pore formation.
Pulsed electric current in SPS produces rapid localized heating at particle contacts.
Localized heating combined with external pressure accelerates diffusion and densification in ZrB2.
SPS refines the ZrB2 microstructure and minimizes residual porosity at lower processing temperatures.
Residual pores serve as nucleation sites for holes during liquid plating-bath exposure.
SPS-processed ZrB2 is expected to achieve near-theoretical density and significantly reduced porosity.
SPS-processed ZrB2 is expected to have greater mechanical strength than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
SPS-processed ZrB2 is expected to be more durable than conventionally sintered ZrB2 during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
Conventional ZrB2 is susceptible to hole formation and degradation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
The proposed service boundary is extended exposure to a controlled-temperature liquid plating bath, for example below 1000 °C.
SPS is known to lower sintering temperatures and improve densification in many ceramic systems.
